clue.text: A variety of larches not seen in the southern states

indicators.note: a variety is a mixed assortment, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A botanical observation that a certain kind of larch does not grow in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A variety of' turns LARCHES plus NOT into the answer. The definition is a little loose: a city of that name is found in South Carolina and West Virginia, and the dance began there.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is a port city in South Carolina, deep in the American South.

clue.text: Figure refuse should fetch money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a figure
ash is the waste residue left after burning

explanation.surface: Someone hoping that rubbish put out for collection will sell for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is a Roman numeral here, and 'refuse' is the noun (rubbish), not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins.

clue.text: He made an effort at sweet talk with some hesitation

parts.note: to sweet-talk someone is to coax or lure them
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A shy suitor tried to charm someone but stumbled over his words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has made an effort is one who has tried, an old word for a trier.

clue.text: Rugby players found at Longleat?

explanation.surface: Asking whether rugby players can be seen at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team; Longleat is an English stately home with a famous safari park full of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The touring rugby side are nicknamed after big cats, and the safari park at Longleat keeps real ones.

clue.text: Tree maintenance

explanation.surface: Looking after a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The service tree is a European tree related to the rowan.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a real species, and a service is routine upkeep of a machine.

clue.text: Harry has got work with the news media

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the press is the collective name for newspapers and journalists

explanation.surface: Prince Harry has had to deal with journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a prince's name; it is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to persecute or harass, as a tyrant does to subjects.

clue.text: The attraction of the lottery

parts.note: one word means both a pulling power that attracts and the moment the winning numbers are picked

explanation.definitionFit: A draw is both something that attracts crowds and the selection of winning tickets.

clue.text: Concerned with private American back-up, point to rule

parts.note: re means regarding, about

indicators.note: in a down clue, back-up means the word goes upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a GI is an American enlisted soldier, a private
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A political sentence about an American soldier's reserve force and governance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' turns GI into IG, between RE and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch.

clue.text: School for the marksman?

explanation.surface: Asking which school would suit a sharpshooter.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester College is an old English public school; the Winchester is a famous American rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both an ancient English boarding school and a classic repeating rifle used by sharpshooters.

clue.text: Getting the timing right, almost everybody will be civil

parts.note: tempo is the timing or pace of music

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Advice that if your timing is good, most people will stay polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civil' here means secular, worldly rather than church; 'almost' cuts the last letter from ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal power is secular rather than spiritual, the sense of civil as opposed to ecclesiastical.

clue.text: A fight to get started

explanation.surface: Starting a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief scrap, and to set to is to begin working in earnest.

clue.text: The salesman allowed one over, thereby giving satisfaction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
let means allowed
I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A salesman let a customer exceed the limit by one, pleasing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Repletion is the state of being full, a feeling of satiety.

clue.text: Leaving out love-letter

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase here, meaning given to omission

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Not sending a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'love-letter' joins two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Omissive describes something that omits or neglects, the act of leaving things undone.

clue.text: There's very little here to steal

explanation.surface: A thief deciding a place has little worth taking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch is a tiny amount of salt or spice, and to pinch is slang for to steal.

clue.text: Romans test materials to make a selection

indicators.note: the two words are raw materials to be worked into something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans testing materials to choose some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' tells you ROMANS and TEST are reworked into a ten-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a mixed collection chosen from various kinds.

clue.text: Delivered plant without charge

parts.note: to set is to plant seeds or seedlings
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A plant was delivered at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' means rescued or liberated, not brought to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delivered from captivity is to be released, made at liberty.

clue.text: Noticed an impression in the grass

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
a mark is an impression left on a surface

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a dent left in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarked can mean observed or took notice of something.

clue.text: Colourful bars

parts.note: reads like lively pubs, but means bands of colour, as on a flag or a sergeant's sleeve

explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands of contrasting colour.

clue.text: Average lot, yet outstanding

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a lot is a quantity, an amount

explanation.surface: A paradox: something average and plentiful that is still excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, more important than anything else.

clue.text: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row

definitions.text: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row

parts.words: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row
parts.note: suggests people whose sport gets them into a quarrel, but row means propelling a boat, and also sitting in a line

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a crew sit one behind another and pull boats with blades.

clue.text: Report ripped up with speed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rip along is to move fast, so ripped means ran
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A report torn up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped up' looks like torn; 'up' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give an account of events, to tell a story.

clue.text: Arranging general increase

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of the next word into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A general organising an expansion of his forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger.

clue.text: Puts on a glossy topper

parts.note: sounds like donning a shiny top hat, but means applying a hard glossy coating

explanation.definitionFit: To enamel something is to coat it with a hard shiny finish.

clue.text: Thin, and so light

explanation.surface: Something both slender and therefore lightweight.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to grow thinner toward one end, and a taper is a slender candle for lighting.

clue.text: Quietly promises to pay, being dutiful

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A debtor quietly writing out promises to pay out of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious once meant devoted to duty, to gods, parents and country, as in Latin pius.

clue.text: Carry on detaining a peer to warn others getting behind

indicators.note: detaining means holding someone inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to ramp is to rage or storm about, to carry on noisily
an earl is a member of the peerage

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene in which a nobleman is held, with warnings to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' means make a fuss, not continue.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light on the back of a vehicle alerts following traffic.

clue.text: A song — Cyril's the composer

indicators.note: a composer puts things together, so the name's letters are composed into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man named Cyril wrote this song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the composer' reads as a songwriter but signals that the letters of CYRIL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem meant to be sung, the words of a song.

clue.text: In the sales some prices are of course lower

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Prices in the sales are naturally reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'sales some'; the remaining words complete the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means smaller in amount, reduced.

clue.text: Egghead individual in extra awkward situation, that's clear

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter E

indicators.note: an awkward arrangement means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: An intellectual finds himself in an awkward spot but is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward situation' mixes E and EXTRA into EXRATE, and 'in' puts ONE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to absolve someone of blame.

clue.text: Excite with sound arguments

indicators.note: sound tells you the word is heard spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: rows are quarrels, rhyming with cows

explanation.surface: Stirring people with well-made arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'valid' but signals a word spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or arouse feelings.

clue.text: Check out note written by holy man

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
St is short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: Checking a note written by a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine or try it out.

clue.text: Through with making cuts — see this causes distress

parts.note: per means by means of, through

indicators.note: making means forming something new, so the letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A surgeon finished with incisions notices the patient is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges CUTS and SEE into SECUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute is to harass and torment someone.
